title: John Powers the City
narrator: Deep, dramatic movie-trailer narrator, friendly, neutral accent. Playful in scenes 1-5, real drama in the storm scenes 6-9.
notes: Each line is placed in its scene so that its 'anchor' word lands on the matching visual event ('anchor_time', seconds from video start). Lines are never moved outside their scene window; if a new voice is too long it is gently time-compressed.

lines.text: If you put John in a giant wheel, he can power the whole house. Sort of.
But spinning alone makes nothing. So you connect it to a generator, with a magnet and copper wire.
But John is too slow to make enough power. So you add gears that make the generator spin much faster.
But the power comes in bumps, and the lights flicker. So you add a battery to store it.
But John gets tired after five minutes. So you dangle a snack in front of him, just out of reach.
Then, the storm hits. Lightning takes out the power station, and the whole city goes dark.
Every house is waiting. And there's only one wheel left spinning.
But at this speed, the wheel starts to burn. So you add water cooling, just like a race car engine.
John runs faster than he has ever run before. And one by one, the lights come back.
Congratulations. John powers the whole city.
